title: A Interior for the Wardrobe
premise: Ivo Dravenmoor, once the conservatory's most celebrated composition prodigy, returns two decades after a public breakdown as a night janitor, content to be unseen. When Mirela Voss, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, asks Ivo to become her final student, they refuse—until discovering that Voss intends to leave her archive, and its power over the conservatory's founding family, to whoever learns it. As Ivo studies under Voss, they uncover that their own mentor's betrayal years ago was orchestrated by the Dravenmoor inheritance itself: a fortune built on silencing the language Voss speaks. In the end, Ivo chooses neither fame nor invisibility but testimony—performing Voss's final song at the conservatory's centennial, naming the theft aloud, and letting the archive pass to a young student rather than themselves.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing endangered-language recordings in Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They live quietly in a coastal town where they teach letterpress printing and insist their best work is done in other people's voices.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Night shifts at the conservatory: mopping stages where Ivo once premiered a concerto, perfecting the practiced smile that deflects former colleagues. Establishes the ritual of invisibility and the old wound—a disastrous debut twenty years ago. Emotional beat: brittle safety, the comfort of being nobody.

chapters.title: A Woman Who Counts in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Mirela Voss begins appearing in the corridors at dawn, singing fragments in an unrecognizable language. She corners Ivo with an impossible request: be my last student. Ivo refuses flatly, but the melody lodges in their head. Emotional beat: irritation masking a dangerous flicker of want.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cleaning the restricted annex, Ivo finds crates of wax cylinders labeled in Voss's language—and a ledger showing the conservatory's founders paid for their suppression. First hint that Ivo's own family name appears in the margins. Emotional beat: dread dressed up as curiosity.

chapters.title: Lessons at the Edge of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Voss POVs. Ivo accepts lessons secretly; Voss teaches grammar through grief, insisting language is 'a house you keep someone alive inside.' Their rapport deepens, but Voss's health visibly fails. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness, the terror of caring again.

chapters.title: The Name on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confirms it: their grandfather funded the suppression campaign, and their old mentor Halvard knew—his betrayal of Ivo's debut was payment for silence. The story Ivo told about their own failure collapses. Emotional beat: vertigo; grief rerouted into fury.

chapters.title: Halvard's Version
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. A confrontation in his office reveals his rationalizations: he protected the institution, and Ivo was collateral. He offers Ivo rehabilitation of their reputation if they help bury the archive. Emotional beat: seductive corruption—the offer of everything except truth.

chapters.title: Voss Failing
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Hospital interludes; Voss races to record what remains, growing furious at Ivo's hesitation to accept the archive. She forces the question: will Ivo inherit the language or merely mourn it? Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into love and ultimatum.

chapters.title: The Centennial Program
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Halvard schedules the centennial gala and plans to announce the archive's 'preservation' under institutional control—effectively entombing it. Ivo realizes time has run out and begins rehearsing Voss's final song in secret, first performance in twenty years. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Climax, Ivo's POV. At the centennial, before donors and cameras, Ivo walks onstage uninvited, sings Voss's song in her language, and names the Dravenmoor theft aloud from the ledger. The room fractures; Halvard's counter-narrative crumbles when Voss, brought by ambulance, confirms it in her own tongue. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: A House Someone Lives Inside
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ivo's POV. Voss dies at peace; Ivo declines the archive, guiding it instead to Lena, a teenage scholarship student who begs to learn. Ivo keeps the janitor's keys but also a teaching hour—no longer invisible, no longer performing. Emotional beat: quiet, earned continuity; survival finally worth its price.
